facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: Chinese wall, which makes a considerable figure upon the terrestrial globe, and may be discerned at the moon.
facts.source_name: The Family Memoirs of the Rev. William Stukeley
facts.text: English antiquarian William Stukeley wrote in a 1754 letter that Hadrian's Wall was surpassed only by the Great Wall of China, which may be discerned at the moon.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: Besides its age it enjoys the reputation of being the only work of human hands on the globe visible from the moon.
facts.source_name: The Peoples and Politics of the Far East
facts.text: English writer Henry Norman noted in 1895 that the Great Wall held the reputation of being the only human-made work on the globe visible from the Moon.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: The Great Wall of China, frequently billed as the only man-made object visible from space, generally isn't, at least to the unaided eye in low Earth orbit. It certainly isn't visible from the Moon.
facts.text: A pervasive modern folklore claimed that the Great Wall of China is the only artificial monument on Earth visible to the naked human eye from the Moon.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: It certainly isn't visible from the Moon.
facts.text: NASA confirmed that the Great Wall of China is impossible to see with the naked eye from the Moon at an average distance of 384,400 kilometres.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: No man-made object is visible at this scale.
facts.text: Apollo 12 astronaut Alan Bean stated that no man-made object on Earth is visible at lunar distances, where only continents, clouds, oceans, and vegetation appear.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Not even the best of human eyes at a simple glace could see the Great Wall of China from space.
facts.text: An optical study determined that resolving the Great Wall from the Moon with unaided human eyesight would require visual acuity 17,000 times sharper than normal.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Now education officials have ordered school textbooks rewritten to remove the decades-old claim that the wall is the only man-made structure that an orbiting astronaut can view with the naked eye.
facts.text: Chinese education officials ordered elementary school textbooks rewritten in 2004 to remove the long-standing claim that the Great Wall can be seen from space.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: In Earth's orbit at a height of 160 to 320 kilometers, the Great Wall of China is indeed visible to the naked eye.
facts.text: Astronaut Eugene Cernan maintained that the Great Wall is visible to the naked eye from low Earth orbit up to 320 kilometres under ideal sunlight, whereas optical scientists and other astronauts dispute this claim by pointing to the limits of human ocular resolution and low contrast against surrounding terrain.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Chiao himself said he didn't see the wall, and wasn't sure if the picture showed it.
facts.text: Astronaut Leroy Chiao captured an orbital photograph of the Great Wall from the International Space Station in 2004 using a 180-millimetre camera lens, confirming that he could not detect the wall with his naked eyes.

intro.prompt: 9:16 vertical, 1080x1920, about 8 seconds, photorealistic and cinematic, bright vivid colour. Setting: view from inside a small spacecraft capsule, an astronaut in a white spacesuit seen from behind pressing close to a round window, below him the vast curved Earth over northern China with brown mountains, winding rivers and desert under harsh sunlight, black space above, dramatic and tense mood. Correction after review: Retag it as something like 'SPACE' or 'MYTH', or drop the tag from the opening frame. Time of day and light, overriding anything darker in the setting above: bright golden-hour sunlight or clear daylight, a blue or golden sky, warm saturated colours, his face and clothes fully lit; never night, dusk, storm clouds, lightning, fog, grey overcast, a dark or desaturated look. The background is real and in motion behind him (as fits the place: waves, mist, leaves, flags, lamps flickering, people walking, traffic, light shifting); never a still, flat or heavily blurred backdrop. If the scene shows the past of an Indian story, it is ancient India (a story from another country keeps that country's own dress and buildings): Indian people in dhotis, sarees and angavastram, warriors with bows, spears and bronze or leather armour, carved stone pillars, oil lamps; never European knights, plate armour, castles or anything medieval European. Movement and framing: like a TV news reporter on location, he walks toward the camera while he speaks: he starts three or four steps back, seen from the knees up, walks steadily and confidently toward the lens, and stops at a medium shot from the waist up for the last words. His whole head and both shoulders stay inside the frame the whole time, with clear space above his hair and on both sides; do not crop the top of his head. Lighting: warm key light on the face, a soft rim light on the hair, matched to the scene; flattering, no harsh shadows, no dull or flat grey look. SG [locked] walking tall and lively, shoulders open, energetic and confident, wearing a navy bandhgala jacket with a white pocket square. Speaks from the first frame, mouth matched to the words, steady eye contact with the lens. Face and delivery: an excited, high-energy presenter breaking a big story, full of life, as if he cannot wait to tell you. Bright, wide-awake eyes, lively eyebrows that lift on the question, a big, bright, genuine smile. On the question his voice rises with excitement as he strides closer. On the last line a big confident smile, a quick nod and a point at the viewer. Natural blinking, lively head movement. Never sad, gloomy, worried, tired, sleepy, flat or bored; never a frown, never a blank face. Voice: energetic, upbeat, punchy and clear, a brisk pace, rising on the question, with a quick beat before the last line. Hands: energetic, natural gestures at chest height: a quick point toward the scene behind him on the question and an open palm toward the viewer on the last line; never limp, never hanging still by his sides. Camera: eye level, steady, holding its place as he walks up to it (a very slight slow push-in at most), slight handheld feel. Empty hands, no prop. @SGMythWorld watermark in the top right corner, white, bold, 80% opacity. No captions, no subtitles, no other on-screen text. No hologram, no floating screen, no graph, no chart, no laptop, tablet, monitor, TV or glowing blue panel anywhere in the frame. Export at 1080x1920.
